reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes buying a Hashflare cryptocurrency-mining contract and directs interested viewers to a description link with a discount code. The solicitation uses a limited-time price incentive and expected Bitcoin growth to encourage financial participation, while acknowledging weak current performance and the possibility of another market crash.

opening.argument: The speaker presents a volatile market discussion with explicit uncertainty, not a promise of profit. He admits that the market may reverse, warns viewers not to copy his own panic-driven trade, and describes the mining contracts as performing poorly rather than guaranteeing returns. That caution is inconsistent with deceptive certification of a safe or profitable opportunity. The Hashflare discussion is framed as a conditional personal decision: he says he may invest, while acknowledging that performance is “not wonderful yet.”

those mining contracts are starting to go up a little bit not wonderful yet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited discount and purchase language shows that Hashflare was mentioned, but it does not establish a guaranteed return or concealed certainty. The same discussion expressly says performance was “not wonderful” and ties the proposed purchase to a conditional market threshold. A limited-time discount can be promotional without being deceptive.

citations.quote: those mining contracts are starting to go up a little bit not wonderful yet
as soon as we get over 10,000 I think it's going to be a good buy

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings about volatility do not neutralize an actionable solicitation. The speaker still tells viewers to use the description link to buy hashrate and says he may put money into the contract before the deadline. Calling performance weak while urging purchase can make the promotion appear candid without showing that the underlying return claim is reliable.

opening.argument: The video is principally commentary and demonstration about cryptocurrency tools and market developments. It explains how Coinbase Commerce and Shopify can be used for online purchases, shows cryptocurrency market data and a Stratis chart, and shares the creator's own trading experience. The Hashflare segment is presented as an example of a current service and its pricing, alongside other platforms, rather than as a proof that viewers will earn money.

citations.quote: Coinbase is working with Shopify now so you can use Shopify to buy and sell, or not sell things but buy things online
So I think that is one of the reasons why the market has gone up so much today is the great news from Coinbase.
I was holding a bag pretty deep and wanted to get out of it as soon as I could

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account isolates the promotional segment and treats the whole video as a purchase pitch. But the supplied material also shows extensive market commentary, a Coinbase-Commerce explanation, and a personal account of a trade that went badly. Those are consistent with technology and financial commentary, and the Hashflare mention can be understood as one topic within that broader discussion.

citations.quote: The other thing that I thought that I am talk about today
this is big news for Bitcoin because now it's making it easier
I could have made some money on that one but now..I got out a loss

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The surrounding commentary does not change the concrete call to purchase mining hashrate. The speaker gives a discount code, states a price comparison, links the service, and says buying would be “awesome.” A video can contain genuine market commentary and still function as a promotional solicitation for the paid mining product.

opening.argument: The observable transaction is ordinary service promotion: a mining-hashrate product is described with a temporary price reduction and a link, alongside links for Coinbase and Minergate. The evidence does not show a guaranteed return, a downline or recruitment scheme, a request for credentials, or a promise that deposits will grow. Even the speaker describes the purchase as a discount opportunity and says current results are not wonderful. That supports ordinary commerce, without certifying the provider as safe.

citations.quote: Hashflare offers Valentines Day Discount, Promo Code: HF18SVALDAY
there is a discount on um hash rate right now
those mining contracts are starting to go up a little bit not wonderful yet

rebuttal.rebuttal: A referral link and a discount code are ordinary features of online commerce. The reference argument calls the price incentive a financial inducement, but it does not identify any guaranteed return, recruitment income, credential request, or fabricated outcome. The speaker instead gives a plainly limited offer and acknowledges uncertain performance.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Ordinary-commerce framing understates the financial context. The product is not merely a retail item: it is hashrate purchased through a mining contract, and the speaker connects its attractiveness to Bitcoin reaching a threshold and urges viewers to use his link. The absence of a guarantee does not make a paid-return solicitation ordinary or safe.
